# Scientific advance: cumulative work and field-shaping change {#sec-session-11}

**Meeting 11 | Tuesday, November 17, 2026 | 1:00-2:00 PM Pacific**

## Central question

What becomes knowable, explainable, measurable, or possible after a contribution, and can we distinguish that gain from attention or prestige?

## The paper pair

**Pairing type:** Empirical indicator / methodological reanalysis.

### Paper A: Large teams develop and small teams disrupt science and technology

@wu2019. **Nature (2019).** [Paper / publisher record](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-0941-9) | [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-0941-9)

Read Wu’s main argument, definition of disruption, and discussion.

*Access: Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.*

### Paper B: The disruption index suffers from citation inflation: Re-analysis of temporal CD trend and relationship with team size reveal discrepancies

@petersen2025. **Journal of Informetrics (2025).** [Paper / publisher record](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1751157724001172) | [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joi.2024.101605)

Read Petersen’s main critique and conclusions. Two discussants examine the index and reanalysis in depth. Dellsén is optional philosophical framing, not a third required paper.

*Access: Open-access journal article; use the 2025 version of record.*

### Why these papers belong together

Wu distinguishes developing and disruptive citation patterns and reports associations with team size. Petersen challenges how citation inflation and reference-list properties affect such inferences. Their disagreement concerns measurement as well as interpretation; neither supplies an uncontested scalar measure of scientific progress. [@wu2019; @petersen2025]

## Prepare before the meeting

Bring one purported turning point and one modest but indispensable contribution. Write a before/after account and initially hide citation counts and journal prestige.

## Discussion questions

1. Can a calibration, correction, archive, or replication be a major advance without an original theory?
2. Is a “big leap” an intrinsic property or a retrospective judgment about consequences?
3. How do entry, authority, infrastructure, standards, and funding shape a field?

## One-hour meeting

| Time | Activity |
|:--|:--|
| 0-10 min | Independent first judgments; surface disagreements. |
| 10-25 min | Compare the papers: claim, evidence, assumptions, and limits. |
| 25-45 min | Work through the case exercise below. |
| 45-55 min | Translate the discussion into agent requirements and tests. |
| 55-60 min | Record an output and one unresolved disagreement. |

### Case exercise

Map prior knowledge -> contribution -> new capability -> later questions for both examples. Mark dependencies, uncertainty, and evidence of actual downstream use. Discuss whether apparent transformation depends on many enabling contributions rather than a single paper.

## Agent-design or evaluation output

Scientific Advance Profile v1: warranted knowledge/understanding/capability gain, contribution role, users, new tests or questions enabled, dependencies, evidence, time horizon, and uncertainty. Keep prospective promise separate from demonstrated impact.

### Working definitions to contest

Novelty is newness relative to prior knowledge; innovation is a new idea, method, or practice that changes how inquiry is done; advance is a warranted gain in knowledge, understanding, or capability; impact is downstream uptake or consequence. These are seminar working definitions, not a universal scale. Incremental, corrective, enabling, integrative, and transformative contributions are roles rather than a hierarchy of personal worth.

## Optional extensions

- @dellsen2016: [Scientific progress: Knowledge versus understanding](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.shpsa.2016.01.003). Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.
- @azoulay2019: [Does Science Advance One Funeral at a Time?](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.20161574). Publisher offers complimentary full-text PDF.
- @wang2017: [Bias against novelty in science: A cautionary tale for users of bibliometric indicators](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.respol.2017.06.006). Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Record after the meeting

Record the evidence for your main claim, what changed your mind, what remains unresolved, and one change to the agent or its evaluation. Keep confidential examples in private group notes rather than committing them to this public book.
